title: @Transactional batch import does not roll back: unchecked vs checked exceptions
errorSample:
org.opentest4j.AssertionFailedError: 실패한 묶음은 롤백되어야 한다 ==> expected: <0> but was: <2>
    at app//org.junit.jupiter.api.AssertionFailureBuilder.build(AssertionFailureBuilder.java:158)
    at app//org.junit.jupiter.api.AssertionFailureBuilder.buildAndThrow(AssertionFailureBuilder.java:139)
    at app//org.junit.jupiter.api.AssertEquals.failNotEqual(AssertEquals.java:201)
    at app//org.junit.jupiter.api.AssertEquals.assertEquals(AssertEquals.java:152)
    at app//org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals(Assertions.java:590)
symptom: A batch insert method annotated with @Transactional throws an exception halfway, but the rows inserted before it are still in the table.
cause: By default Spring rolls back only for RuntimeException and Error. If the failure is not treated as a rollback-triggering exception, the transaction commits whatever was written before it.
fixSummary: Declare the rollback rule explicitly on the annotation: @Transactional(rollbackFor = [Exception::class]). With every exception type triggering rollback, rows written before the failure are discarded.
